sources.role: Not an OpenMS header. BSpline2d is a PIMPL wrapper around this vendored library, so the library is the real implementation this port had to reproduce.
Domain, boundary-condition and basis declarations; documents the Ooyama formulation and the node-count heuristic.
solve/evaluate/slope; the mean-subtraction and the evaluation window are ported from here.
Setup, Alpha, Beta, Basis, DBasis, qDelta, calculateQ, addP. Holds the truncated PI, the float accumulators and the out-of-range Beta reads.
Explicit template instantiation for float and double; fixes T = double for OpenMS.
Banded storage plus LU_factor_banded and LU_solve_banded; the out-of-band scratch element and the pre-update zero-pivot check come from here.

fixtures.role: The BSpline2d class test's data: x = seq(-5,5,0.1) plus Gaussian noise, y = 10*sin(x) plus noise, resampled with replacement and re-ordered by x, so abscissae repeat. Used for the 202-point fit whose 405 coefficients are compared one by one.

stdout of the probe built from ../oracle/msc_splines/main.cpp with the recorded flags, one `case<TAB>key<TAB>value` row per observation at %.17g. Covers 12 CubicSpline2d positions with all three derivative orders, the class test's sine grid, seven error paths, 17 BSpline2d configurations with every node coefficient (including the degenerate two-node grid under all three boundary conditions and the three-node grid), the class test's mean-squared-error assertions, 31 BSplineSmoothingSpline fits (including the four that pin the candidate sort) and 10 spline_bisection brackets. The first 1693 rows are byte-identical to the output recorded at a965767; the 135 rows after them were appended by calling the two new case groups at the end of main().

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)
Target: arm64-apple-darwin25.6.0
Thread model: posix
adaptations: OpenMS/config.h, OpenMS/OpenMSConfig.h, CONCEPT/Types.h, CONCEPT/Macros.h, CONCEPT/Exception.h and CONCEPT/LogStream.h are shims: an empty OPENMS_DLLAPI, Size/UInt typedefs, an inert OPENMS_PRECONDITION as in a release build, a std::runtime_error-derived Exception::IllegalArgument, and an OPENMS_LOG_ERROR that writes to a discarded ostringstream so stdout stays machine readable.
No MATH/MISC translation unit and no eol-bspline file is modified; BSplineLib.cpp instantiates the templates exactly as the OpenMS build does.

The driver additionally constructs eol_bspline::BSpline<double> alongside each OpenMS BSpline2d so the node count, node domain, penalty weight and basis coefficients that the PIMPL wrapper hides are observable.

The driver was extended at this commit with degenerate_cases() and candidate_sort_cases(), called after the original four groups so every row printed before them is unchanged. They probe num_nodes == 2 and the BSplineSmoothingSpline candidate sort; the scientific translation units are still unmodified.

determinism.note: A second build at -O0 with the same -ffp-contract=off produced byte-identical output (sha256 8db7798a77984df139c28a6fae810801bc54de9bfe25dbf6594ec6f1e1fdad71).

floating_point_contraction.note: The same sources built without -ffp-contract=off, which is clang's default on arm64, differ in 1234 of the 1828 recorded values because multiply-adds are fused into FMA. The earlier description of that difference as 'one or two units in the last place' was wrong and is replaced by the measured distribution: median relative difference 8.9e-15, 300 values above 1e-13 relative, 35 above 1e-12, with the largest gaps on values of ordinary magnitude being 9.7e-9 relative (bspline_ramp_asc eval@0) and 1.7e-10 (bspline_solve eval@0). Fourteen rows differ by order unity and every one of them is numerically zero - the residual sum of squares of an exactly fitted line or parabola, or the curve's value at a zero crossing. The banded normal equations amplify a fused rounding into a coefficient difference around the fourteenth digit. The strict build is the recorded oracle because it is what a compiler without FMA contraction produces and is therefore reproducible on any target; see docs/BSPLINE2D_SUPPORT.md.

cpp_probe.assertions_disabled: -DNDEBUG is load-bearing for the num_nodes == 2 cases: on the two-node grid BSplineBase::Beta is called outside the range its own assert(0 <= m && m <= 3) permits, and the same sources built without -DNDEBUG abort there instead of returning a spline. A release build is what OpenMS ships, and the values the probe records do not depend on what those out-of-range reads returned, because every one of them is consumed by a write the banded storage discards.

class_test_review.note: Every START_SECTION of the four class tests is reproduced by a named Rust test; docs/*_SUPPORT.md name the test and one concrete asserted value per section. Two groups of probe cases go beyond the class tests: the degenerate two- and three-node BSpline2d grids, and the four BSplineSmoothingSpline fits that pin the candidate sort.

source_anchors.operation: adjacent_find with std::greater accepts equal neighbouring abscissae, which then divide by a zero interval width in init_
eval steps back one knot when lower_bound overshoots or when x is the last knot, so the last segment is evaluated at its right end
c_.back() = 0 and the recurrence leaving c_[0] = 0 are the natural boundary condition
PI is the truncated literal 3.1415927, which feeds Alpha
Setup rewrites a zero cutoff wavelength to 1.0, so the derivative constraint is never actually disabled
the node search starts at ten intervals, so an automatic node count with a positive wavelength needs at least eleven points
calculateQ holds b1, b2 and the accumulator in float, rounding the boundary correction to single precision
the lower-right boundary loop calls Beta(M-4), which reads BoundaryConditions[bc][-1] when M < 4; the result is written to a banded coordinate that discards it
addP holds every basis value and every product in a float before accumulating into the double normal matrix
the ordinate mean is subtracted before the fit and added back in evaluate, which is why evaluation far outside the domain returns the mean
evaluate sums only the four basis functions around the query node and clamps the window to [0, M], so the sum is empty beyond two node intervals
LU_factor_banded tests the pre-update diagonal for zero, then divides by the post-update one
LU_solve_banded divides by A(M, M) without the zero check the rest of the loop performs
a polynomial fit is accepted when its residual sum of squares is within ten percent of the budget, which is why a coarse fit can beat an exact one

the candidate comparator is not a strict weak ordering, so which candidate std::sort leaves at position zero is unspecified and differs between standard libraries; the oracle is libc++, whose __introsort switches on the range length and sends three, four or five elements to the __sort3/__sort4/__sort5 networks rather than to an insertion sort. The port's stable insertion sort is pinned against the executed libc++ result by the smooth_tie_break and smooth_cycle probe cases.
lefthand_sign is seeded true and never updated, reducing the exclusive-or to the sign of the midpoint derivative
the do/while has no iteration cap and does not terminate when the midpoint stops moving

calculateQ calls Q.setup(M+1, 3) and ignores the result; BandedMatrix::setup refuses N_ < abs(first), so for two nodes the matrix keeps its default 1x1 shape and the fit proceeds on a one-row system, leaving the second coefficient unsolved

the right-hand side and the solution are the same vector, sized M+1, while LU_solve_banded takes its dimension from A.num_rows(); on the two-node grid those disagree and A[1] keeps the accumulated right-hand side

native_boundaries: CubicSpline2d requires strictly increasing finite abscissae; the source accepts non-decreasing ones and then produces NaN coefficients.
BSpline2d and BSplineSmoothingSpline return Err where the source leaves an object whose ok() is false; BSpline2d::ok stays for the post-construction solve failure the source can still reach.
BSpline2d caps input at 250 000 points and 500 001 nodes, so the banded matrix never exceeds 28 MiB; the source bounds neither.
spline_bisection caps the loop at 4 096 halvings and requires a finite positive threshold; the source can loop forever.
Every evaluation and every recurrence intermediate is checked for finiteness, so a non-finite result is an error rather than a silently propagated NaN.

calculateQ skips the (i, j) pairs the C++ computes from an out-of-range Beta and then discards; the discarded-write argument is in docs/BSPLINE2D_SUPPORT.md and the result is numerically identical, on the two-node grid as well as for M <= 3.
No OpenMP: the source carries no pragma in these four files, so there is no parallelism gap to record.

num_nodes == 2 is reproduced, not refused: the source's failed Q.setup leaves a 1x1 matrix and still returns a finite spline whose second coefficient is an unsolved right-hand side, and the port returns the same numbers. The type documentation states plainly that it is not a fit.
